4.text: outer shoulder has to work harder than the inner one. This form of harness

5.text: was introduced from the south. It is in use among the Amur tribes, as may

7.text: everywhere in Kamchatka, and in the countries farther to the north it is

8.text: therefore called the Kamchatka harness. The usual harness of northern type

9.text: (Fig. 25, b) has two cross-bands and a single or double trace (Fig. 25, c).

10.text: Those of the finest style even have a third narrow cross-band (Fig. 25, d).

32.text: the dogs’ places from time to time, according to the change in their disposition

34.text: The southern drivers cover their dog-harness with colored paint, and adorn

35.text: it with red flannel and embroidery (Fig. 26, a). The Chukchee do not make

36.text: such harness themselves, but gladly buy it from the Russianized natives of

37.text: Anadyr. The Asiatic way of attaching dogs, when compared with North

38.text: American methods, has its advantages for travel on land, especially in the

39.text: woods, where the path is narrow and winding. With short traces fastened to

40.text: a central strap, it is difficult for the animals to jump around any tree standing

41.text: close to the road, as they would do with the long Eskimo traces. Even on
